summary: Digital-interaction bizStep vocabulary is OUR draft superset extension of GS1 CBV, never ratified GS1.

declaredDebts.note: All 4 digital bizSteps (Resolving, Requesting, Scanning, Viewing) are draft/provisional Vin superset terms. They mint the gs1.org.ai/cbv/BizStep-<gerund> shape and are openly marked NOT ratified GS1 CBV. Every rendered surface (the .data description and the GS1/cbv/[BizStep].mdx banner) must carry that marking.

Rendering (render View) is EXCLUDED and deferred out of scope: it is a presentation-layer concern, not a business-context state transition. Held here rather than shipped. Revisit only if #105 explicitly rules it in.

Scanning's down-projection is conceptual-only. No ratified CBV bizStep for AIDC code capture (no BizStep-reading exists in CBV), so sameAs is intentionally left EMPTY — no ref.gs1.org target was fabricated. Same for Resolving and Requesting (pure superset). Only Viewing carries a real down-projection: ref.gs1.org/cbv/BizStep-inspecting (verified ratified in .source/GS1/cbv-ontology.ttl).

Digital rows use id=BizStep-<gerund> and code=bizstep-<gerund> — a hyphenated, lowercase-after-hyphen form that intentionally deviates from the Wikipedia-style ID convention. This is the #105 canonical URI shape (gs1.org.ai/cbv/BizStep-<gerund>), a DISTINCT namespace from the physical EPCIS/BusinessStep/{code} path. validate.test.ts flags such IDs as warn-only, so the suite stays green.

blockers.note: The #105 ruling text is NOT present in this worktree. The gs1.org.ai/cbv/BizStep-<gerund> URI shape and the down-projection-to-ref.gs1.org convention are taken from the task brief and MUST be confirmed against the actual #105 issue before merge.
